chunks: Hammād ibn ʿĪsā narrated from Ibrāhīm ibn ʿUmar al-Yamānī, who attributed the statement to ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib (peace be upon him), that he would say:

The best things through which the supplicants can entreat Allah are: faith in Allah and His Messenger, jihād in the way of Allah, and the word of oneness (kalimat al-ikhlāṣ) — for indeed it is the innate nature (fiṭrah); establishing prayer — for indeed it is the creed (millah); giving the zakāt — for indeed it is part of what is obligatorily due to Allah; fasting in the month of Ramaḍān — for indeed it is a shield from His chastisement; pilgrimage to the House — for indeed it alleviates poverty and wipes away sin; maintaining ties with near of kin — for indeed it is a means of increasing one’s wealth and delaying one’s death; giving charity in secret — for indeed it does away with sin and extinguishes divine wrath; and [doing] good turns — for indeed they repel tragic death and protect [one] from falling into disrepute.

Ensure that you are [always] honest, for Allah is with the one who is truthful, and turn aside from falsehood, for indeed lies take one away from faith. Know that the truthful one is close to salvation and honor, while the liar is on the brink of humiliation and destruction.

Speak [only] what is good and you will be known for it, act upon it and you will become one of its folk. Return the trust to the one who entrusted it to you, and keep ties with the near of kin and turn towards them in kindness.

key_terms.صَوْمُ شَهْرِ رَمَضَانَ: Fasting in the month of Ramadan

ai.seo_question: What are the best acts of worship and ethical conduct for drawing near to Allah according to Imam Ali?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Kitab al-Zuhd* presents Imam ʿAlī’s (peace be upon him) comprehensive taxonomy of spiritual practices, linking each act of worship to a worship to its metaphysical consequence, such as fasting being a 'shield' and kinship ties increasing lifespan. It emphasizes the foundational role of truthfulness (*sidq*) as the bridge between faith and salvation, a concept central to Shia ethical theology. The narration concludes by integrating ritual obligations with social ethics, urging believers to fulfill trusts and reciprocate kindness, thereby harmonizing the individual’s spiritual state with communal harmony.
